cohort: 248 pregnant mothers attending antenatal clinics at St. John's Medical College Hospital, India, between November 2018 and November 2020.
finding: Increased maternal BMI was strongly associated with preeclampsia, GDM, cesarean delivery, and larger babies, while underweight women had higher chances of preterm delivery and NICU admission for their infants.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery rates were higher in women with increased BMI.
birth_weight: Larger babies were born to mothers with increased BMI
